title: Dell Technologies Stock Hits a New All-Time High: Is It Too Late to Buy?
author: David Jagielski, Cpa
description: Dell Technologies stock has surged over 320% year-to-date, hitting an all-time high, driven by strong demand for AI servers. Despite the impressive gains, the stock's valuation remains reasonable with a trailing P/E of 31x and forward P/E of 21x (in line with S&P 500 average). The company reported 58% revenue growth and more than tripled net income in its most recent quarter. Analysts suggest the stock could continue rising as businesses invest heavily in AI infrastructure.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Dell has demonstrated exceptional financial performance with 320% YTD gains, 58% revenue growth, and tripled net income. The stock's valuation (31x trailing P/E, 21x forward P/E) is reasonable relative to growth rates. Strong demand for AI servers and continued business investment in AI infrastructure support a bullish outlook with potential for further appreciation.

title: Dell Booked More AI Server Orders in 3 Months Than It Recorded in Total Revenue
author: Daniel Sparks
description: Dell Technologies received $60.9 billion in AI server orders during Q2 FY2027, exceeding its total quarterly revenue of $47 billion. The company exited with a record $95 billion backlog and raised full-year revenue guidance to $192 billion (69% growth). However, operating cash flow declined to $2.2 billion despite tripled net income, raising concerns about Dell's ability to convert orders into delivered systems and collect cash on schedule.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Record AI server orders ($60.9B), exceptional revenue growth (58% YoY), tripled EPS, and raised full-year guidance to $192B (69% growth) demonstrate strong demand and execution. Stock surged 12% to 52-week high. However, sentiment is tempered by cash flow concerns and execution risks on converting backlog.

title: Nike Is Being Deleted From the S&P 100. Is Its Seat in the Dow Jones Industrial Average in Jeopardy?
author: Daniel Foelber
description: Nike has been removed from the S&P 100 effective September 21 as part of quarterly rebalancing, marking a significant decline for the company. With stock prices at 12-year lows, declining revenue and earnings, and operating margins plummeting, Nike is now the lowest-ranked component in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, putting its membership in jeopardy. The article suggests investors should wait for concrete signs of a sustained turnaround before buying the stock.

title: Quantum Up 322% in the Past 6 Months: Time to Buy, Hold or Sell?
author: Na
description: Quantum Corporation (QMCO) shares have surged 322.3% in six months, driven by strong enterprise demand for ActiveScale and tape storage solutions. The company reported 25.7% revenue growth to $80.8 million in fiscal Q1, with expanding tape adoption and improving margins. However, supply constraints, particularly for tape drives, limit near-term revenue conversion, with Q2 guidance at approximately $82 million.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 25.7% YoY revenue growth, significant stock appreciation (322.3% in 6 months), expanding enterprise adoption of ActiveScale and tape solutions, improved gross margins (39.3%), positive cash flow, and debt elimination. Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating supports positive outlook despite supply constraints.
